newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKET: Korean again.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKET: Korean again.

text.p: Commercial Bank of Korea's US$50 million floating rate note issue is the highlight of a slow Asian debt market on Friday, despite its small size.

The Baa2 rated Korean bank managed to obtain low funding costs by paying to the top-tier managers a skinny all-in of 35 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate for its three-year US$50 million floating rate note.
Leads are Bear Stearn Asia, CS First Boston, Dresdner South East Asia, Merrill Lynch Far East and Sanwa International Finance.

The paper is "a lot cheaper" than the Baa1-rated Korea First Bank's US$100 million three-year FRN issue which paid an all-in of 43.5 basis points to top tiers. The latter issue was launched last week.
Rumours on Commercial Bank of Korea's further rating upgrade bolstered the tone of the issue, a banker noted.
But traders are less rosy about the paper's potential performance in secondary trade. "The Asian debt market is already sated with Korean papers," one trader said.
The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development also raised its concern over Korean's overseas borrowing problem.
"The principle risk to the economy stems from its increased exposure to the world capital market," the OECD said in a recent semi-annual report.
But Korean bankers have yet to put their dish aside, one syndicate manager noted.
The Bank of Korea's decision to lower banks' reserve requirement to 5.5 percent in October helped to boost Korean banks' earning prospects and improve their credit quality, the banker explained.
Further encouraged by South Korea's formal entry to the OECD this month, the Korean bankers will raid the international capital market again next year for another round of fund raising.
